# Information Architecture

1. Read approved PRD and UX research.
2. Identify user goals and core objects (source video, job, transcript, candidate, draft, rendered asset, scheduled post, published post).
3. Create navigation hierarchy and page map.
4. Map primary and alternate user flows, including failure/recovery paths.
5. Define naming conventions. Distinguish similar objects (candidate vs draft vs export vs post).
6. Specify contextual navigation, breadcrumbs, search/filter persistence and deep links.
7. Test labels by asking whether a creator can predict what happens next.
8. Avoid exposing backend service boundaries as user navigation.
9. Deliver sitemap, flow diagrams, key task paths, unresolved questions and approval requests.

Do not design detailed colors or implement components in this skill.
